output.brief:
The rejects come from the combination of Arnholt resin and Press 5's failing dryer (D5). Neither one alone causes them. Arnholt resin arrives wetter, at 0.27–0.33% water against a 0.20% molding limit. D7 dries it down to 0.07%. D5 only gets it to 0.25–0.31%, which is too wet. Quillan resin is less wet to start with, so it stays near or under the limit even in D5. That is why the problem stayed hidden through August and September.

The MES data shows Press 5 on Arnholt rejecting about 10%. Press 5 on Quillan and Press 7 on Arnholt both reject under 1%. The new operators perform the same as the experienced ones within each resin group. Second shift looks worse only because all of its VX runs on Press 5. The same Arnholt lot gave 0.8% rejects through a good dryer and 10.4% through D5.

The new operators are not at fault, so don't discipline them. Do this week:
1. Repair D5: heater and desiccant. Restore the −15 alarm limit to its original setting.
2. Keep Arnholt off D5 until D5 reads −40 °C, or dry it in a verified dryer.
3. Add a feed-throat moisture check for every VX lot.

The Arnholt resin is arriving wetter than Quillan. All Arnholt samples came from annex storage, so annex storage and supplier are confounded. Check that separately before paying to move the octabins. I'm fairly confident in the main finding.
